heading: C. Wright Mills, “The Promise”

works.cite: C. Wright Mills, “The Promise,” in The Sociological Imagination. Oxford University Press, 1959.

tie: Mills separates personal troubles, which happen inside one person's life, from public issues, which come from how a society is organized. He argues that people can only understand their own lives once they see that link.

A student who decides computer science "isn't for me" seems to be making a private choice. When the same choice shows up across whole groups of students, year after year, it is a public issue. This site treats enrollment, admissions and hiring numbers that way.

heading: Brown v. Board of Education and “The Problem We All Live With”

works.cite: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka, 347 U.S. 483 (1954).
Nikole Hannah-Jones and Chana Joffe-Walt, “The Problem We All Live With,” Parts One and Two, This American Life, episodes 562 and 563, July 31 and Aug. 7, 2015.

idea: Access to a school is not the same as equal outcomes inside it
tie: Brown ruled that segregated public schools violate the Equal Protection Clause. Sixty years later, Nikole Hannah-Jones reported on the Normandy School District in Missouri, the district that includes Michael Brown's high school, where a transfer program opened better-resourced schools to its students and that access was fought over.

Stage 01 of the pipeline counts whether a school offers computer science. The rest of the diagram asks what happens after that door opens: who is placed in the class, who is pointed toward the AP exam and who reaches the next step. A course in the catalog is where the question starts, not where it ends.

heading: Bettina L. Love, “Grit, Zest, and Racism”

works.cite: Bettina L. Love, “Grit, Zest, and Racism,” in We Want to Do More Than Survive: Abolitionist Teaching and the Pursuit of Educational Freedom. Beacon Press, 2019.

idea: Don't blame students for dropping off
tie: Love argues that teaching grit asks students of color to endure conditions that racism created, and treats their survival as a character trait instead of changing the conditions.

When a dot falls off in the diagram, it is easy to read it as a student who didn't try hard enough. The log records where students leave, not why any one student did. The question at each stage is what about the school, the course or the policy pushed students out.

heading: Center on Education Policy, “For the Common Good,” and Milton Friedman, “The Role of Government in Education”

works.cite: Center on Education Policy, George Washington University, For the Common Good: Recommitting to Public Education in a Time of Crisis, 2020.
Milton Friedman, “The Role of Government in Education,” in Robert A. Solo, ed., Economics and the Public Interest. Rutgers University Press, 1955.

idea: Who education is for, and who should pay for it
tie: CEP argues that public schools serve public purposes, not only private ones, and makes the case for recommitting to a strong public system. Friedman argues that government is justified in paying for general education because an educated public benefits everyone, a "neighborhood effect," but not for "purely vocational education" that mainly raises one student’s earnings.

Most events on this timeline are arguments over that line. Supporters of the rollback say public money and public colleges should not favor some groups over others. The programs being cut were built on the idea that widening who studies computer science is a public good, not only a private investment.

heading: This course is taught under Senate Bill 1

works.cite: ESPHE 3206 (School & Society) course syllabus, The Ohio State University, “Intellectual Diversity” section.

tie: The ESPHE 3206 syllabus cites Senate Bill 1 under Intellectual Diversity. SB 1 requires Ohio State and every other state university to post course syllabi publicly and to "ensure the fullest degree of intellectual diversity."
The rollback on this page is not only something that happens at other schools. It shapes how this course, the one this site was made for, describes itself.
